We have three templates returned. Need to find which matches our target molecule and gives a mapped_rxn that is applicable. The target molecule is given with atom mapping numbers. We need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule, reproduces the reaction (i.e., forward carbonyl-ene). The search gave templates with mapped_rxn fields. We need to check which template matches our molecule. Likely the first one (reaction_id 1209837) seems to involve a carbonyl-ene? The retro_smarts_template: '[C:3]-[C:2](-[C:4])-[OH;D1;+0:1]>>C-C(=C)-C(=O)-[O;H0;D2;+0:1]-[C:2](-[C:3])-[C:4]'. That seems like reverse of carbonyl-ene (product is alcohol, reactant is enone). Our target molecule has a hydroxyl attached to a carbon bearing CF3 groups etc. The mapped_rxn includes many atoms but seems to have the product as the alcohol (our target). So likely template_id is the reaction_id? Actually we need template_id (the one used to search the database not the hash). The returned dict includes 'reaction_id' and 'template_hash'. The template_id likely corresponds to reaction_id? In earlier tasks, template_id is integer like 3421. So we should use reaction_id as template_id. So choose the best match with highest similarity maybe 0.387. So template_id = 1209837. Mapped_rxn is given. We need to output that mapped_rxn string. Let's extract mapped_rxn from first entry.

Mapped_rxn: 
'CCCCCCCCCCCCS.CC(C)(C#N)N=NC(C)(C)C#N.C=C(C)C(=O)[O:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][CH2:4][CH:5]([C:6]([OH:7])([C:8]([F:9])([F:10])[F:11])[C:12]([F:13])([F:14])[F:15])[CH:16]([OH:17])[CH2:18]1.CCC(C)=O>>[OH:1][CH:2]1[CH2:3][CH2:4][CH:5]([C:6]([OH:7])([C:8]([F:9])([F:10])[F:11])[C:12]([F:13])([F:14])[F:15])[CH:16]([OH:17])[CH2:18]1'

That seems to include extra reagents (CCCC..., etc) which are not part of our molecule. Might be a generic template with side reagents. Might still be applicable.

But we need to ensure the template matches our molecule. Could test with check_smiles_reaction_template_matching but we don't have template_id for that. We have reaction_id. The tool expects template_id string. Might be same as reaction_id. Let's try check matching with first template id 1209837.
